note: S1-F033's proposed intermediate representation between raw input and model consumption; this review finds it single-sourced, unquantified, and outside the Kernel boundary by existing law.

The observation that Kernel-inclusion arguments split into two types -- cost/economics arguments (reward more Kernel content) and invariant/protection arguments (reward less/minimal Kernel content) -- which can yield opposite verdicts from the same evidence; flagged as a standing caution across the Session-2 review register.

A structure described (l.208 of an out-of-batch source) as carrying 'the delimiting conditions... the frame beyond which the claim is incomplete'; offered as a candidate answer to whether v1.1 models context sufficiency, not merely context presence.

A Session-2 register (established on HPA direction, 2026-08-25) of observations about relationships BETWEEN tracks (extraction methodology, review methodology, research findings, formal architecture, adjudication) -- never mixed with corpus findings, never routed automatically into adjudication. Entries numbered X-nnn, kept separate from the S2-Fnnn finding series.

The claim that Assessment, Observation, Evidence, Recommendation and Decision are mutually irreducible categories (not merely sequenced, per KCON-003), used to support but not resolve an assessment/relationship split (S1-F014).

The finding that KnowledgeOS v1.1's Authority member is a bare Reference with no temporal binding (0/20 examined grants carry temporal properties), while the claim it admits carries a full TemporalValidity interval -- so a revoked authority's past admissions become permanently unauditable, an irreversible loss not protected by any existing invariant. Verdict: IMPLEMENTATION QUESTION, pending whether the Authority supporting context internally holds grant validity intervals.

S1-F036's central proposal: the minimum unit KnowledgeOS must preserve is an identity-bearing, contextualized assertion record; called by the review the corpus's most reusable positive result, surviving an atomicity falsification untouched. Distinguished from, and not to be collapsed with, a consistency boundary or a projection view (three formerly-conflated roles that both used the word 'aggregate').

note: The five-indexed positive epistemic-honesty formulation KnowledgeOS can guarantee in place of correspondence-truth: an assertion was evaluated as X under regime R, in context C, at time T, based on evidence E. Distinguished explicitly from relativism; consistent with law's rejection of a truth oracle.

A membership test (if a capability is removed and preservation/reconstruction of identity and epistemic history remains possible, it probably does not belong in the Kernel) materially identical to the reviewer's own standing 'Kernel test' instruction (same HPA authorship, not independent convergence); applied by S1-F036 to 24 candidate items with 2 honestly left undecided -- the only place in the corpus where a membership criterion is actually executed.

Four candidate scalar operators (MAX, weighted mean, noisy-OR/SATURATING, naive-Bayes-style BAYES_LIKE) for aggregating evidence-item strengths into a single epistemic scalar, evaluated under RAW (no preprocessing) vs PIPE (dependency-collapse plus relevance-filter before aggregation) semantics against eight designed properties (A-H) from an earlier design (20260827-134514) and verdict (20260827-135038); GN-27 adjudicated a CSV-vs-verdict discrepancy, and GN-46 is an independent recheck reproducing that reasoning without modifying either artifact.

A ratified admission ladder (Candidate -> Supported -> Accepted) with a Committed decision boundary enforced as a strict covering relation (I-12): no skipping, and the boundary is crossable only by an authority act (A6/I-4), never by evidence volume. Adjacent FA layered states (REJECTED/CONFLICTED) are reachable only by a governed act and are preserved in history, never deleted. An expressibility probe against a source model (Omega_A = Support/Acceptance/Commitment/Contest) finds a residue: no single layered-model state can jointly express Accepted plus an active Contest (the PF-6 residue).

A strict-conjunction admissibility rule for Decision Contracts (no averaging across Pre/Invariant/Assurance/Authorization or a six-fold refined form; any False component forces False; any Unknown component forces Block/None, never True). A formal mismatch is reported: the ratified six-tuple Decision Contract has no ratified admissibility conjunction of its own (the four-conjunct early form omits Temporal; the six-fold refined form belongs to a different seven-tuple), and the six-tuple has no component typed as epistemic sufficiency (Q), making a Q-based block inexpressible without conflating it into Evidence (PF-7's loss).

note: A verse-by-verse speculative mathematical formalization exercise mapping all of Bhagavad-gita Chapter 4 onto proposed KnowledgeOS structures (epistemic lineage/decay, memory, intervention trigger, reward, role-based duty, non-attachment/bondage, dual-state action/inaction, a wise-person state vector, multiple evidence pathways, epistemic benefit/purification, teacher-student learning, and faith/doubt/closure), each paired with a sketched Python implementation, culminating in an integrated GitaKnowledgeOS class and a single closing equation KnowledgeOS = Wisdom*Action/(Doubt+Attachment). note: The corpus's only complete falsification cycle: a v0.1 proposal that 'projection = measure' was refuted six independent ways (at four distinct levels plus one attacking the completeness claim itself) in about 78 minutes and resolved by its own proposer into 'relational/logical structure as the mathematical core, with metric/topology/probability/measure/statistics/causal models as regimes'. Rated by Session 1 the best-evidenced episode in the corpus; confirmed by Session 2 as demonstrating a perspective-diverse attack pattern never applied to the corpus's own Kernel formulations, and as resolving specifically because the proposer (not an outside party) performed the refutation and resolution.

The GN-46 independent mathematical/statistical/computational verification report (extending GN-43), auditing the entire ratified KnowledgeOS mathematical content under a strict verify-not-repair mandate. Produces a 16-object mathematical inventory, definition/derivation/computability/statistical/metric/measure/entropy/topology/operator audits, an independent EXP-01 recheck, a source-vs-synthesis compression audit, and 22 findings (MV-F-1..22, including newly registered ones: status-set non-closure MV-F-3, an unregistered EC compression member MV-F-4, a missing ratified admissibility law for the ratified Decision Contract MV-F-5, a type-incorrect PROPOSAL-to-DECISION flow edge MV-F-6, and a consolidated 'identity calculus' gap MV-F-22). Final verdicts: boundary/invariant layer sound with qualifications, formal-object layer under-specified, system not computationally realized, statistical content sound by abstention.
